lesson.subtitle: Lesson 9 -- Advice for a Young Manager

lesson.grammar_point: third conditional (if + had + past participle, would have + past participle) and mixed conditionals (past cause, present result)

listenings.text: People sometimes ask me what the turning point of my career was, and the answer always surprises them. It was the day I was laid off. I was thirty-two, working at a bank in London, and I was devastated. But if I hadn't been laid off, I would never have started my own business. I'd probably still be sitting at a desk in that bank, or retired from it. So with hindsight, it was the best thing that ever happened to me. Do I have regrets? One. When my children were young, I worked far too much. If I had taken more time for them then, I think I'd be closer to them now. I stepped down last year, at seventy, and that's the advice I give every young manager.

Here's what I see again and again. People quit on a bad day. They're exhausted, they're burned out, and they walk into their manager's office and resign. And six months later they say: if I'd waited a little, if I'd had a plan, it would have been so different. So before you quit, ask yourself three questions. One: am I leaving something, or am I going to something? Two: do I have a safety net? Three: have I actually talked to my manager? You'd be surprised how many problems can be solved with one honest conversation. And one last thing. The research is very clear: people regret the risks they didn't take much more than the ones they did.

I was an engineer in the car industry for twenty-five years. Then, at fifty, I decided to quit and open a bakery. Everybody thought I was crazy. Was it a risk? Of course. But I weighed it up for two years, and I had a safety net: my savings and my wife's salary. Today I have a small bakery in Lyon, and I've never been happier. Would I do anything differently? Yes, one thing. If I had found a mentor before I started, someone with experience in the business, I wouldn't have made so many mistakes in the first year. I lost a lot of money that I didn't need to lose. So find a mentor. It's the cheapest insurance in the world.
